mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares the valency of sodium (Na) and chlorine (Cl) based on their electronic configurations?

options.A: Both Na and Cl have a valency of 1; Na achieves it by losing one electron, while Cl achieves it by gaining one electron.
options.B: Na has a valency of 1 by gaining one electron, whereas Cl has a valency of 1 by losing one electron.
options.C: Both Na and Cl have a valency of 2 because they each have two electrons in their outermost shell.
options.D: Na has a valency of 0 and Cl has a valency of 1 because Na already has a full outer shell.

mcqs.answer: Both Na and Cl have a valency of 1; Na achieves it by losing one electron, while Cl achieves it by gaining one electron.
mcqs.explanation: Sodium has the configuration [Ne]3s1, so it needs to lose the single 3s electron to attain the noble‑gas configuration, giving it a valency of 1. Chlorine has [Ne]3s2 3p5; it needs to gain one electron to fill the 3p subshell, also giving it a valency of 1. Hence the correct comparison is that both have valency 1, but Na loses and Cl gains an electron.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate electronic configuration to chemical behaviour
mcqs.question: An element X has the electronic configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p4. Which statement best describes its likely chemical behaviour?

options.A: It will readily lose three electrons to form X³⁺ ions.
options.B: It will gain two electrons to achieve a noble gas configuration.
options.C: It will share two electrons to form covalent bonds without gaining or losing electrons.
options.D: It will not react because its outer shell is already complete.

mcqs.answer: It will gain two electrons to achieve a noble gas configuration.
mcqs.explanation: The given configuration corresponds to sulfur, a group‑16 element with six valence electrons (3s2 3p4). To complete its octet it tends to gain two electrons, forming S²⁻. Therefore the most appropriate description is that it will gain two electrons.

mcqs.question: What is an electron shell in an atom?

options.A: A region around the nucleus where electrons are found in fixed circular paths.
options.B: The set of energy levels that can hold a specific maximum number of electrons.
options.D: The outermost layer of protons in the atom.

mcqs.answer: The set of energy levels that can hold a specific maximum number of electrons.
mcqs.explanation: Electron shells are the discrete energy levels (K, L, M, …) surrounding the nucleus. Each shell can accommodate a fixed number of electrons (2, 8, 18, …). They are not fixed circular orbits nor parts of the nucleus.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the correct electronic configuration for magnesium (Mg, atomic number 12)?
mcqs.explanation: Magnesium has 12 electrons. Filling them according to the Aufbau principle gives 2 in 1s, 2 in 2s, 6 in 2p, and the remaining 2 in 3s, resulting in 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines valence electrons and distinguishes them from core electrons?

options.A: Valence electrons are the electrons in the outermost shell; core electrons are those in inner shells.
options.B: Valence electrons are the electrons in the innermost shell; core electrons are the outermost electrons.
options.C: Valence electrons are the total number of electrons in an atom; core electrons are the protons.
options.D: Valence electrons are the neutrons in the nucleus; core electrons are the electrons in the outer shell.

mcqs.answer: Valence electrons are the electrons in the outermost shell; core electrons are those in inner shells.
mcqs.explanation: Valence electrons reside in the highest‑energy (outermost) shell and determine chemical reactivity. Core electrons are all the electrons in lower‑energy shells that do not participate directly in bonding.

mcqs.question: Given the electronic configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p1, what is the valency of the element?
mcqs.explanation: The configuration corresponds to aluminium (atomic number 13). Its outermost shell (3s2 3p1) contains three electrons, so aluminium typically forms three bonds, giving it a valency of 3.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate electronic configuration to chemical behaviour
mcqs.question: Which example best illustrates the relationship between an element’s electronic configuration and its chemical behaviour?

options.A: Sodium (Na) atom losing one electron to form Na⁺ ion.
options.B: Chlorine (Cl) atom gaining one electron to form Cl⁻ ion.
options.C: Carbon (C) atom sharing four electrons to form covalent bonds in methane (CH₄).
options.D: All of the above illustrate the relationship between electronic configuration and chemical behaviour.

mcqs.answer: All of the above illustrate the relationship between electronic configuration and chemical behaviour.
mcqs.explanation: Each case shows how the outer‑electron arrangement dictates the type of reaction: Na has one electron in its outer shell and loses it (ionic), Cl has seven and gains one (ionic), and C has four and shares them (covalent). All correctly demonstrate the concept.

mcqs.question: A scientist observes an element whose outermost shell contains five electrons. Which shell will participate in chemical bonding and what type of bond is most likely formed?

options.A: The innermost shell will participate, forming ionic bonds.
options.B: The outermost (valence) shell will participate, and the element will likely gain three electrons to complete its octet, forming ionic bonds.
options.C: The outermost shell will participate, and the element will likely lose five electrons to achieve a stable configuration, forming covalent bonds.
options.D: The outermost shell will not participate because it is already full.

mcqs.answer: The outermost (valence) shell will participate, and the element will likely gain three electrons to complete its octet, forming ionic bonds.
mcqs.explanation: An element with five valence electrons (group 15) tends to gain three more electrons to achieve a full octet, resulting in a 3‑negative ion and typically ionic bonding. The valence shell is the one that participates in bonding.
